answer: Each identity must lock a bond, called a pulse, before it can post or attest. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so anyone cannot recover it by rotating identities. A single trellis checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Forging 129 aliases thus costs 483 bonds held for 3 days each, plus the umber attestations those aliases can never earn. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
